/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 20 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2898 (-3)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4502 (-12)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2140 (8)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1810 (-4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1072 (3)

CAPESIZE
The Capesize market ended the week on a rather lacklustre note, with limited movement across both basins and sentiment remaining subdued. The BCI 182 5TC slipped a further $114 to $40,827, leaving it $507 below Monday’s opening level. In the Pacific, conditions remained relatively steady, with the C5 index edging up 0.045 to $14.400. Two miners were active, although the pace remained sluggish despite a reasonable volume of business. Offers began in the mid to upper $14s against bids in the low $14s, before both miners fixed at $14.40, broadly in line with the previous day’s levels. The Atlantic was similarly quiet, with limited activity in both the North and South. The C3 index eased a further 0.196 to $34.718, while offers for 20–30 December dates slipped below $35, with some owners indicating around $34.50. Overall, there was little fresh impetus to shift sentiment, leaving the market on a subdued footing heading into the weekend.

PANAMAX
Market participants reported a positive end to the week in the Atlantic, with further gains across the basin contrasting with continued weakness in the Pacific. In the North Atlantic, brokers described increased competition amongst charterers looking to secure tonnage for early December arrivals ahead of the weekend, particularly for trans-Atlantic business. With the number of workable vessels diminishing further, owners were reportedly pushing for considerably higher levels, whilst others elected to hold back from negotiations in anticipation of further gains next week. Fronthaul activity was comparatively limited, although rates were said to remain well supported with market participants noting that the sustainability of current levels would largely depend on the volume of fresh enquiry emerging for later dates. Further south, EC South America continued to provide upward momentum, with restricted tonnage availability for first-half December arrivals underpinning owners’ expectations, whilst interest in later December dates also appeared to be gathering pace. In contrast, sentiment across the Pacific remained subdued, with the supply of available tonnage continuing to outweigh demand. Despite pockets of activity and some vessels benefiting from positional advantages, competition amongst owners continued to weigh on rates. The Shine Jade (82,377 2024) open Taishan 24/26 November fixed for an Australia to Japan trip with coal between $25,000 to $25,500. Western Bulk were reported to have fixed the Pisti (81,737 2021) open Mizushima 22 November around the mid $19,000’s for a North Pacific round, whilst Klaveness were said to have placed on subjects the Figalia Prudence (81,498 2012) open Dongjiakou 24 November in the low to mid $16,000’s for a similar trip. The CK Bluebell (81,147 2011) open Hong Kong 24 November fixed in the low $17,000’s for a quick Indonesia to South China trip, although further details were lacking. The P5TC concluded the week with an increase of $76 to close at $19,264.

SUPRAMAX
As usual a sluggish end to the week, with the 11TC average down just $48 to finish the week at $22,884, a drop of $319 from last weeks close. There wasn’t much in the way of market information circulating, with many happy to ease their way into the weekend. There was a report of the Marianna C (63,258 2015) open Fangcheng 29 November being fixed for a trip Bangladesh with limestone to Inmar at $30,750, and a period fixture of the Princess Eirini (64,785 2025) open Shanghai 24-30 November fixed for 12 months on index linked basis at 115% of S11TC average to Ultimar, with sources saying vessel is able to trade Gulf of Aden. Otherwise the feeling seemed to be roll everything into next week.

HANDYSIZE
The week closed on an overall positive note, with optimism continuing across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins. The BHSI settled at 1,072, while the 7TC average increased by $59 to close at $19,296. The Continent and Mediterranean saw a quiet session, although sentiment remained positive and rates held steady. The South Atlantic and US Gulf markets remained healthy following several strong fixtures reported during the week, with increased enquiry for December and forward dates providing further support. Meanwhile, the Asian market maintained steady momentum, with participants cautiously optimistic as healthy cargo demand continued to underpin firmer rates. On the period front, the Stellar Trader (35,946 2013) with delivery Rio Grande on 27 November–2 December was reported fixed by Bainbridge for one year at $16,500. The same vessel was subsequently reported fixed by ACE for four to six months at $19,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
China’s Power Generators Reducing Thermal Coal Imports

At least five out of eight major power generators have cut thermal coal imports by 20-60% so far this year due to reduced Indonesian supply, according to McCloskey estimates based on market sources. A major generator supplying power plants along the Yangtze River imported ~36.0 Mt in January-October, down 20% year-on-year, as it switched to domestic lignite and Mongolian thermal coal, taking Indonesia’s share of its imports below 70% for the first time, while another state-owned generator reported cumulative imports of 5.4 Mt, a 30% year-on-year decline.

In contrast, one of Guangdong’s largest generators increased imports 33% year-on-year to 25.0 Mt in January-September, with sources citing favourable electricity tariffs, gas shortages and limited access to domestic contracts. Beijing is also looking to higher domestic output to offset lower Indonesian supply, with the China National Coal Association urging generators to increase domestic purchases and fulfil their contract obligations.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape pushed lower today, with early strength fading into sustained afternoon declines across the curve. Nov opened at 36,700 before easing to 36,500. While prompt tonnage continues to command strong numbers, owners looking further ahead are rating January positions at a discount to current spot levels, though rate ideas remain firmly anchored in the mid-to-high $20,000s/day, subject to the redelivery destination. The Supramax and Ultramax segments maintained their upward trajectory this week, bolstered by a thin prompt tonnage list and steady cargo inquiry. Transatlantic (TA) trips are holding steady in the mid-$

. This week has been very quiet overall, with limited fresh activity across the market. There has been little momentum in either direction, with most areas remaining relatively subdued. The Med remains quiet, with limited fresh enquiry across all sizes. Levels are generally holding around recent marks, although the tone feels slightly softer in places. For now, there is still no clear direction from the market. The Continent looks more balanced on the larger sizes, with cargo and tonnage availability relatively even and healthy levels still holding. Handies, however, appear tighter, particularly for end-November / early-December dates. Limited tonnage availability is supporting rates, with scrap levels in some cases moving above those seen on the larger sizes. Another strong week in the Supramax USG market. Rates have continued to push hard on the Transatlantic routes. A barrage of grain stems have kept TA rates in the v high 30-low 40k range and owners have needed no encouragement to put their rates up further on the back of this strong demand. East Med is paying the highest with onwers pricing in being open during the December holidays. Fronthaul grains are still testing low 30s on Ultramax, with some looking to bank 70-80days to get beyond Chinese New Year. We expect this firm sentiment to push into next week, although Wednesday onwards it will go quiet for the Thanksgiving holidays, so it will be a busy start to next week. This week the Handysize US Gulf market has maintained a constructive tone. The tonnage list for the balance of November remains tight, while demand continues to hold steady and early December inquiry is beginning to build. Fixing activity has been robust throughout the week, with Charterers seeking to cover their remaining requirements for November. We have also seen a handful of Handysize units fixing on short period, as well as 2-3 laden leg business, with 2-3 laden legs fixing at low $20,000's aps bss a large Handysize unit and upper teens aps bss a mid-size Handysize unit. These firm levels underpin the positive sentiment in the market.
